No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The lecture examines what made a city more than four thousand years ago: planning, drainage, standard weights, seals and trade. Setting the Harappan cities beside their contemporaries shows what the early civilisations shared and what was distinctive to the Indus.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • What makes a settlement a city
  • Planning, drains, weights and seals in the Indus cities
  • Mesopotamia, Egypt and early China beside the Indus
  • The Indus script, which no one has yet read

How the time is spent

  1. Urban plans 20 min

    Dholavira, Mohenjo-daro and Harappa comparisons.

    You: map features

  2. Economy 45 min

    Crafts, exchange and farming patterns.

    You: artifact cards

  3. Big questions 25 min

    Differences among Indus settlements and decline debates.

    You: claims-v-evidence board

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Explain what makes a settlement a city, using planning, drainage, weights and seals.
  • Compare the Indus cities with their contemporaries in Mesopotamia, Egypt and early China.
  • Distinguish claims from evidence in debates on differences among Indus settlements and their decline.
